docs.title: Skylords Reborn Blender Artist Guides
docs.text:
Create and export models with SR-ImpEx. These guides describe the development build.

Start here: Static Object Guide — edit an existing DRS, create your own model, or bring in a foreign model.

  • Default Material Guide
  • Unit Creation Guide
  • Building Creation Guide
  • Advanced Shading Guide
  • Advanced Locators Guide
  • Advanced Abilities Guide
  • Advanced Effects Guide

docs.title: Advanced Abilities Guide
docs.text:
Configure attack, casting, and channeling animation metadata after completing the Unit Creation Guide. For timed audio and visual resources, use the Advanced Effects Guide; for attachment points, use the Advanced Locators Guide.

Scope: an entry called an “Ability” in this editor maps a visual job to an animation. It does not create a gameplay ability, projectile behavior, damage, targeting rules, cooldown, or resource cost. Those must already be configured in the game's data. The workflows below concern DRS export. For a building's root AnimationSet and state resources, use the BMG package workflow.

docs.title: 1. Know Which Data You Are Editing
docs.text:
Data What it contains Where it is authored Blender Action / .ska Bone motion and clip timing Action Editor; Clip Settings for timing metadata AnimationSet Visual job (vis_job), mode, weighted Action variants, clip segments, markers Animation Set Editor AnimationTimings Timing category/tag, variant index, millisecond timings, direction, marker reference Generated through the editor's per-variant Timing section EffectSet Audio/FX references scheduled against a named SKA clip EffectSet panel Locators Model or bone attachment points CDrwLocatorList Editor

An animation marker, a locator, and an EffectSet keyframe are separate records. Matching their time or position does not automatically link them or create an in-game event.

docs.title: Choose a Starter Layout
docs.text:
Click Init, choose Model Type, then confirm:

Model type New entries Static Object None. Wind and flowing textures do not need skeletal animation clips. Animated Object Idle Unit Idle, Walk, Run, Spawn, Die Building Idle if the model has an armature; none for a static building

Existing mappings are kept. Enable Replace Existing Mappings only to clear the list first; it does not delete Actions. New entries have no Action assigned. Choose an Action for each entry you need, then click Save.

These are small starting layouts, not a universal list required by the engine. For an animated unit, always assign a usable Idle in Base mode: several actions use it as a fallback. A file loading successfully does not guarantee safe playback when that fallback is missing. A fallback Idle does not replace the intended walk, spawn or death motion. Add attack, hit, mode-change and other animations when the existing game configuration uses them. Building damage states and construction are configured through the building tools, not by this template. The type choice does not change the export type or create gameplay behavior.

An animated prop may need only Idle. The Animated Object DRS export types retain only Idle and remove animation markers and timings. Use Animated Unit when the exported model needs attack/cast mappings and timing data. Units and animated objects need an armature before initialization.

docs.title: Basics: Motion in the Game
docs.text:
For a unit, open Basics. Keep the imported settings unless you intend to change its motion. These settings are exported; Blender's Play previews the Action and does not simulate the game's movement, terrain or hit reactions.

Setting What it changes Walk / Run Reference Speed The movement speed each clip was authored for. The game adjusts playback to movement and model scale, and uses the midpoint of these two speeds to choose walk or run. This does not set gameplay movement speed. Use positive values; zero prevents that movement clip from starting. Partial Mode Change Runs the mode-change animation alongside the main animation. Disabled: the mode-change animation becomes the main animation. This needs the game's mode setup and a matching animation mapping. Align to Terrain Tilts a ground unit to the terrain slope. The flying motion path skips this alignment. Flight → Hovering Ground Unit Uses the hovering/flying motion path for a unit near the ground, including lean and hit offsets, with different death-trajectory handling. It does not make the unit fly in gameplay or set its height. Flight → Turn Banking How strongly a flying unit leans in a turn. Zero removes this contribution. Flight → Movement Pitch How strongly a flying unit tilts with its movement speed and acceleration. Zero removes this contribution. Flight → Hit Displacement Strength of a flying unit's spatial hit response. Zero removes this offset, not its hit animation.

New sets use reference speeds 2.3 / 4.8, Turn Banking 2, Movement Pitch 0.4 and Hit Displacement 1. The three checkboxes start disabled. Existing values are retained.

Dragging uses convenient ranges: 0–10 for reference speeds and 0–5 for flight scales. These are editing ranges, not engine limits; you can type other finite values. Negative flight scales can reverse a contribution. The file stores 32-bit floats and the loader does not impose a general 0–1 clamp. Unit motion settings are hidden for other initialized model types; Debug View makes them available when needed.

docs.title: 2. Work Safely in the Animation Set Editor
docs.text:
Select your model or its root collection, then open 3D Viewport → Sidebar → DRS Editor → Animation Set Editor. When switching between models, save the current model's edits first and use Reset to load the newly active model's stored data.

Control Actual behavior Init Choose a model type and add its starter mappings. Keeps existing entries unless Replace Existing Mappings is enabled. Remove All Clears the working list. Save afterward only if that removal is intended. Save Writes working state to the active collection's AnimationSetJSON; does not export files or save the .blend. Reset Reloads the active collection's stored data, discarding unsaved editor changes. Mode Filters entries by mode. Labels include Base, Special, Rest, and Rest->Base when present. Add Ability… Adds catalog components in the current mode; existing (vis_job, mode) pairs are not added twice. Ability-row minus button Removes that mode-key entry. Grouped rows should be checked carefully after removal. Variant + / − Adds/removes variants of the selected entry.

Save a backup before editing imported metadata: the editor reconstructs its supported schema, not every possible unknown field in an original file.

docs.title: 3. Choose an Existing Visual Mapping
docs.text:
Use the catalog label matching the model's existing game-side behavior. These are actual catalog entries, not new gameplay ability definitions:

Catalog label Visual-job components Timing category / tag Attack MeleeAttack (8); catalog describes it as melee or ranged Melee / 0; marker required by the catalog Special Melee Attack Ground SpecialMeleeAttack (15) Melee / 114; marker required Special Melee Attack Air SpecialMeleeAttackAir (16) Melee / 115; marker required Cast (Ground Only) CastGround (18), CastResolve (19) CastResolve / 0 Cast (Ground & Air) Ground 18/19, Air 22/21 CastResolve / 0; catalog requires identical ground/air timings PreparedSalvo Ground 185/186, Air 187/188 CastResolve / 54 SpecialRangedAir Cast 316, Resolve 317 CastResolve / 148 Harpoon Cast 321, Resolve 322 CastResolve / 150 Heal Channel Start 177, Loop 178, End 179 Channel / 48

There is no generic catalog entry named Ranged Attack. A regular ranged model can use the existing Attack visual job; a specialized model may use one of the named cast/resolve mappings. The timing label Melee on Attack is not a gameplay switch that makes an attack melee.

Ground-only and ground/air cast entries share visual-job IDs, so they are not independent sets of interchangeable slots. Display labels are inferred from the catalog's ID map and can resolve to the shared ground/air label after reloading.

Mode switching is not a supported recipe. The catalog explicitly calls its entry ModeSwitch (Not yet Supported). SwitchToSpecial and SwitchToNormal are internal component roles sharing job 7, not independent supported animation types. Although ModeSwitch exists in the timing-category enum, that alone does not implement a complete transition workflow. Preserve known working data rather than treating the presence of a label as proof of support.

docs.title: 4. Assign and Check Every Variant
docs.text:
1. Add the matching catalog entry in the intended mode.
  2. Select a variant and choose its Action. The dropdown includes Actions from the entire .blend, not only the current model. Its shortened display label is not necessarily its datablock name or exported filename.
  3. Give each intended variant a weight. 80 and 20 is a useful two-variant convention. Animation weights are individually limited to 0..100 in this UI, but the editor does not normalize their sum or reject totals other than 100. Do not assume a particular engine selection algorithm from the percentage display alone.
  4. Review Allows IK and Force No Blend. New variants default to enabled and disabled respectively; they are metadata flags, not Blender rigging or baking commands. Keep established imported settings unless a deliberate change is needed.
  5. Preview each variant. Play uses the selected variant, not a weighted random sample.

A variant with <None>/an empty Action is skipped when constructing the exported AnimationSet. Merely creating an Action or NLA strip does not add it to an ability mapping.

docs.title: 5. Place Markers and Understand Time Units
docs.text:
The catalog enables the Marker section for Spawn, Attack, and selected special mappings. Casting entries normally use Cast→Resolve instead; a marker section is not available for every ability.

Control Meaning in the current editor Time Fraction of the full Action, 0..1; not seconds or a Blender frame number Is Spawn Animation Stored marker flag; seeded for Spawn, not a general gameplay activation toggle Position Stored XYZ event position; choose it against the pose at the marker time Direction Stored direction vector; also orients the display arrow Play Marker Plays from the Action's start to the normalized marker time Display Marker Assigns the Action, jumps to the marker pose, and shows its arrow in DRSMarkers

For a five-second clip, marker 0.6 is at three seconds. To place an event at 0.6 seconds in that clip, use 0.12. EffectSet keyframe times use the same normalized 0..1 convention, so matching fractions aligns the scheduled moments only when both refer to the same full clip.

Keep these editor units separate from unverified game-tick behavior. Historical notes about 100-ms quantization, a 200-ms Spawn minimum, a six-entry limit, and resolve-phase duration are research hypotheses, not confirmed authoring rules. See AnimationTimings research status before interpreting exported millisecond fields.

For a weapon or hand event, inspect the pose with Display Marker, then edit the marker's numeric Position/Direction. Markers are not bone-bound locators, and dragging the helper arrow is not a supported “sync back” workflow: the stored UI values remain authoritative. A marker can be near a projectile attachment point, but neither creates nor automatically links that locator. Retain imported armature/locator parenting; do not reparent bones or locators just to match the helper arrow.

docs.title: Generated Millisecond Timings
docs.text:
The Timing section shows read-only Type, Tag ID, Is Enter Mode, VariantIndex, Cast (ms), Duration (ms), Used FPS, and MarkerID; its Direction remains editable. Change clip timing and the normalized marker/split controls rather than attempting to type new millisecond values.

For timing recomputation, the editor uses the Action's frame_length and original_fps when available, otherwise its frame-range span and effective scene FPS (fps / fps_base). In this implementation:

  • Duration (ms) / exported resolve_ms is the full clip duration.
  • Exported cast_ms is that duration multiplied by marker Time, or by Cast→Resolve when no marker is present.

These are the add-on's calculations, not proof that a specific game-side damage/projectile event uses either field in a particular way. Some older format documentation describes different meanings and editable timing fields; the current editor code is authoritative for these controls.

docs.title: Cast or Ranged Release Example
docs.text:
1. Use the existing model's mapping: for example Attack for its regular attack or Cast (Ground Only) for an existing generic cast hook.
  2. Assign the full clip, including preparation and follow-through.
  3. For Attack, set marker Time at the visual release/contact pose. For a cast pair, set Cast→Resolve at the transition you want to inspect.
  4. Use Play Cast and Play Resolve to inspect the two ranges of the selected full Action. Resolve rows are hidden in the main ability list.
  5. Configure the required locator separately, then add audio/FX keyframes to the corresponding clip in EffectSet.
  6. Save, export, and test in the game configuration that actually invokes this visual job. A plausible preview does not create a functioning spell or projectile.

Action selection is propagated between corresponding Cast/Resolve entries. Ground and air channels are separate; explicitly verify their clips and matching timings rather than assuming one edit updates both.

docs.title: Loop Set Example
docs.text:
For PushBackStandUp, Heal Channel, or another catalog Start/Loop/End group, the UI shows one Loop Set row. Use a full clip with a preparation, repeatable middle, and exit. Set Start.end and Loop.end, then inspect the Start, Loop, and End preview buttons. Selecting an Action propagates the same variant index's file across the group.

Range caveat: linked Action selection and preview buttons are not a guarantee that every hidden component's exported Start/End values have been synchronized. Current drawing logic updates only the first Start/Loop variants' ranges, and cast previews compute their Resolve range separately. Reimport and check the exported component ranges, especially End/Resolve and additional variants, before relying on segmented playback.

docs.title: 7. Prepare the Actual Export Action
docs.text:
A control rig is an authoring aid; the deform/game armature supplies the exported skeleton and motion. The preview helpers can prefer an armature named Control_Rig, while the SKA exporter explicitly excludes armatures containing that name. Successful control-rig playback therefore does not prove that the export Action contains usable deform-bone motion.

The SKA writer reads the selected Action's bone location and quaternion rotation F-curves. It does not bake evaluated IK/constraints, the NLA stack, Euler rotation, or scale into motion automatically. Bake/convert the intended final motion onto the deform armature's bones before export when the source relies on those systems. Preserve the existing skeleton/rest-pose relationships and bone names; the writer derives bone IDs from known names or its fallback name hash.

New clips can start at a later frame: export subtracts the clip's recorded first frame before normalizing its key times. After moving the keys, use Edit Settings → OK to update the recorded range.

Use Animation Set Editor > selected animation > Clip Settings > Edit Settings to set per-Action FPS, first frame, duration, time addressing and interpolation. OK automatically derives the range from existing keyframes while keeping the imported clip's leading/trailing time; no separate fit button is needed. Timing edits do not rescale or bake F-curves. FPS and frame length determine duration. Imported frame_length, original_fps, and original_duration can override later scene changes, so review Clip Settings after changing the keyed range. Playback matches the selected clip's scene FPS and timeline limits. Settings belong to the Action and are shared by all variants that reference it.

The last stored key is not necessarily the clip's end. For example, Firedancer Idle1 has 78 samples at 24 FPS and lasts 3.250 seconds, even though its last key is at frame 77. Loop playback uses frames 0–77; including frame 78 would add an extra frame every loop. The preview enables Frame Dropping to keep real-time speed when Blender cannot draw every frame.

Looping tracks continue smoothly from their last key back to their first key. Each bone's last key can occur well before the clip ends. The plugin creates boundary copies to show this motion in Blender, refreshes them when the active Action changes, and leaves them out of SKA export. Edit the original keys rather than these generated copies. After updating the plugin, Play also repairs loop previews in older imported Actions.

docs.title: SKA Metadata Is Not an AnimationSet Mode
docs.text:
The full track/keyframe path in the current SKA reader/writer is implemented for file types 6 and 7. New SKA exports are generated as type 7; a research template describing types 2–5 does not establish equivalent add-on support for them.

  • Track headers distinguish position (0) from quaternion rotation (1) and bind tracks to skeleton bone IDs. Renaming a clip does not retarget its skeleton.
  • Each keyframe stores four values and four tangent components. This layout is not a generic export path for arbitrary Blender scale, Euler, or constraint animation.
  • Both supported layouts store duration, repeat/stutter metadata, frame length, and trailing integers; type 7 includes an extra integer before frame length. Do not assign guessed meanings to unknown fields. This is not a lossless byte-for-byte rewrite: the current exporter generates three trailing zeros, so keep the original clip as a reference.
  • The writer uses the Action's repeat value when present, otherwise 0, and its stutter_mode when present, otherwise 2. These file-level settings are distinct from AnimationSet's Start/Loop/End clip ranges.
  • Historical notes call frame length “unused” or describe particular stutter values as smooth. Those engine effects remain unverified. The add-on still uses frame-length/FPS metadata for timing calculations; do not discard it or treat it as a guaranteed in-game speed control. Use Clip Settings and round-trip the result.

docs.title: 8. Save, Export, and Round-Trip Check
docs.text:
1. Inspect every mapping/variant and its timing section, then click Save in both AnimationSet and EffectSet. Save the .blend too.
  2. Export a DRS as Animated Unit for these unit visual mappings.
  3. Enable Export All SKA Actions when new SKA files are needed. Despite its name, this exports clips referenced in the saved AnimationSet blob, not every Action in the file. An EffectSet-only Action reference does not by itself schedule an SKA export. Unresolved Actions can be skipped.
  4. Choose Model Name Prefix deliberately: No Prefix, Model Name Prefix, Folder Name Prefix, or Keep Existing Prefix. The DRS dialog currently defaults to No Prefix, not Model Name Prefix. The naming map rewrites AnimationSet, marker-set and EffectSet animation references together, replacing spaces and resolving filename collisions; check actual output names rather than predicting them from dropdown labels.
  5. For smooth keyed motion, review [DEBUG] Export SKA Tangents (enabled by default in DRS export). The standalone SKA exporter selects one Action and has its own Export Tangents toggle, defaulting to off. Tangents cannot recover missing/baked-out motion.
  6. Reimport the output into a clean test scene and compare clips, mapping IDs, variants, ranges, timing values, marker position/direction, and effects against the source. Finally verify the game-side behavior with its existing ability definitions.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Checklist
docs.text: Symptom Check first No attack/cast mappings after export Animated Unit type, correct active root, editor Save, nonempty Action assignments; Animated Object intentionally filters these out. Missing or incorrect SKA Saved AnimationSet references, actual Action names, output prefix, ambiguous/truncated names, and exported files. The resolver can fall back to similar prefixes. Motion works only on the control rig Bake deform-bone location/quaternion channels; the writer does not export the evaluated rig/NLA result. Wrong speed or shifted release Per-Action timing metadata, effective FPS, zero-based keyframes, normalized Time versus seconds, and full-clip versus segment timing. Loop/resolve replays the wrong part Reimport and inspect all hidden component ranges and variant indices; preview splits alone are insufficient. Marker display is right but game event is wrong Compare exported marker IDs to AnimationTimings references and confirm the game actually invokes the intended job/tag. Marker-set IDs are regenerated on Save separately from timing IDs; do not assume those links round-trip unchanged. Existing data changes after Save Work on a copy; schema reconstruction is not lossless preservation of unknown fields or unsupported mappings.

docs.title: Advanced Effects Guide
docs.text:
Use Effect Set Editor to attach existing effects and sounds to a model's animations. Create new effect assets in the external Effect Editor.

For building damage, use BMG Editor â†’ Building Editor â†’ Build Damage Preview. Its Damage slider combines mesh states, scratch, destruction debris and FX. See building damage preview.

docs.title: 1. Set Up the Asset Library
docs.text:
Open Edit â†’ Preferences â†’ Add-ons â†’ SR ImpEx.

  • Set Skylords Reborn Folder to your game installation.
  • Optionally set Effects Folder to a loose effect library, such as Mods/Unpack/bf1/gfx/effects. Use this to preview your own assets before installing them.

Choose the game installation folder containing base/pak, rather than the pak folder itself. Both library paths are saved automatically and restored after Blender restarts, even when Blender's automatic preference saving is off. Leave the optional Effects Folder empty if you only use game assets.

The add-on also keeps a shared settings copy outside Blender's version-specific profile. It can recover the paths when that profile is reset or replaced. Clearing a path deliberately clears the saved value too.

The library reads existing files. It prefers loose assets and can find effects and sounds in the game's current PAK archives. It does not modify the game files.

The first search builds a file index and saves it in your user cache. It is reused across models and Blender restarts. Searches and preview builds check file-system metadata: changed folders are scanned again, and changed PAK directories are read again. Unchanged archives are not unpacked or reindexed. All current archives in base/pak are eligible, including building assets.

Refresh Effect Library forces a fresh index if needed. Corrupt or outdated cache data is rebuilt automatically. The cache contains filenames and archive locations; textures, meshes and sounds are loaded only when needed.

docs.title: 2. Add an Animation Event
docs.text:
1. Select a mesh belonging to your imported model.
  2. Open DRS Editor â†’ Effect Set Editor.
  3. Add an entry and choose its Action. Each entry belongs to one SKA animation.
  4. Add a keyframe and choose its Type below.
  5. Set Time (0..1): 0 is the clip's start, 0.5 its middle and 1 its end.
  6. Add a resource variant. Open Effect Selector, search by name, and click Use Resource. You can also enter the filename directly.
  7. Keep one variant at Chance 100% while testing.
  8. Click Save, then save your .blend separately.

Changing the Action retargets the entry. Imported sound containers and header data are retained when you save, although the panel does not yet let you edit every sound container.

Group filters the shared resource picker using name/path hints such as Fire/Smoke, Water/Ice, Persistent/Ambient and Buildings/Destruction. Resources can belong to several groups. Choose All Resources when unsure. The same picker and preview library are available in Locator Editor.

docs.title: Choose the Event Type
docs.text:
Type Use Sound Play a sound resource. World FX Spawn an effect at the model's position at that moment, with an offset. Linked FX Use an effect whose setup follows source/target nodes. Attachment depends on the effect itself. Fade Out Persistent FX Fade an existing locator effect with the matching resource name. Fade In Persistent FX Fade an existing locator effect with the matching resource name back in.

Fade events operate on an existing effect; they do not spawn another copy. Their Fade Duration (s) controls how long the fade takes.

For ordinary events, Offset adjusts placement. It does not select a bone or replace a locator. Reuse a working model/effect setup when you need a particular attachment behavior.

docs.title: Resource Variants
docs.text:
Variants are alternative resources for the same event, not simultaneous layers. For two alternatives, use chances such as 80 and 20, totaling 100. The engine does not scale these numbers automatically: 4 / 3 / 3 means 90% silence or no effect, while 40 / 30 / 30 always selects one. The panel shows the unused chance. Normalize to 100% scales the current proportions when you want an event every time; imported values stay unchanged until you edit them. Avoid totals above 100, which can make later variants unreachable.

To play two effects or sounds together, create two events at the same Time, each with its own resource variant.

docs.title: 3. Check the Resource
docs.text:
Open Effect Selector. Search at the top or choose a category on the left. Categories such as Fire, Water and Buildings are hints from filenames, not engine effect types.

Select a resource and click Preview to audition it on the model. The existing FX preview is paused during the audition and restored when you close the selector. Cancel keeps your original resource; Use Resource puts the selection in the editable filename field. Save the EffectSet or locator separately to include it in export.

Sound events show audio resources instead of FXB files. Missing or ambiguous references produce an error when previewing.

docs.title: Play the Effects in Blender
docs.text:
In Object Mode, click Update Preview, then press Space to play the normal scene timeline. Choose an animation entry to preview its scheduled effects. Persistent building/unit locator effects can also be previewed when there is no animation entry. Rebuild after the current render finishes.

  • Audio includes sound cues. Multiple cues can overlap. Sound-set loops repeat through the preview range.
  • Engine Chances uses the saved chances. The preview makes repeatable random choices without adding an exported seed setting.
  • Selected Variant auditions the highlighted variant of the highlighted event, even if its chance is zero. Other events keep their normal chances. This changes only the preview.
  • Clear Preview removes generated effects and their audio strips for this model. It leaves your model and unrelated audio alone.
  • Live Update is on by default. After the first Update Preview, changes to the selected clip, event timing, volume, pitch, FX offset or variants update automatically after a short pause in editing. Playback stays running at its current frame. Large effects can pause briefly while rebuilding; updates wait until rendering finishes. Clear Preview stops live rebuilding. Rebuild the preview after reopening a saved .blend.

A clip without assigned effects is normal: the preview reports this as information. The same applies when Audio is off for a sound-only clip, or when the preview picks the unused part of the event's chances. Missing files and effects without supported preview components remain errors; the message names the resource, and the model's Effect Preview Report in Blender's Text Editor contains details. A persistent locator effect does not need an imported Action unless you also preview timed animation events.

For sound events, Pitch Min/Max are rate shifts: 0 leaves playback unchanged, 0.1 adds 10%, and -0.1 subtracts 10%. The preview picks a repeatable value between them. Both pitch and sound duration change. Values must produce a positive playback rate to be previewed.

Controls marked Export Only are saved for the game but do not affect the Blender preview: falloff needs positional audio, Interruptible needs gameplay animation interruptions, and Stored Condition is retained without a verified filtering effect in this timeline path. Editing these fields does not rebuild the preview. Use the Map Editor to check gameplay-dependent behavior.

Generated previews live outside the model's export collection. They are not exported as extra meshes. Do not edit those generated objects; edit the model's EffectSet or the original effect in the external Effect Editor.

Switching to another model or importing a new model stops the previous model's preview audio. Sound strips you added yourself are kept. Build the selected model's preview again to hear its effects.

Cycles transparency depth is adjusted automatically for overlapping effect sprites, and restored when the last preview is cleared. Very dense overlaps can reach Blender's hard limit; the preview report lists this case. This setting fixes early ray termination without changing the material's transparency.

Legacy flame emitters, including Firedancer's head and hands, use smooth transparency automatically in EEVEE. They should look like soft overlapping flames rather than a cloud of dotted pixels during playback. After updating the add-on, click Update Preview to rebuild older preview materials. The source textures and exported effects stay unchanged.

docs.title: What You Can Check
docs.text:
Part of the effect Blender preview Lights, billboards and nested effects Placement, animation, color and opacity. Light brightness is approximate. Effect meshes Geometry and the supported DRS material shading. Animated effect meshes also play their SKA through the effect's animation curve. Default refraction meshes sample the background in camera renders and follow the FX fade. The viewport uses a simpler refraction shader. Material animation Supported scalar and color curves drive the existing material preview. Parameters without a visual route are listed in the report. SFP particles Starting colors, size, lifetime, rotation, weighted atlas tiles and render ramps. Particles keep their placement at emission and use the stored mass and system damping. Counts, random sampling and reduced motion caches remain bounded approximations. Legacy emitters and satellites Legacy emitters use traced particle motion, color, opacity, size and supported blend controls. Each component follows its own activation window. Distortion-only particles do not produce colored flames; their heat haze is not reproduced. Scene fog and satellite-specific motion remain incomplete. SFP force fields Cached attraction, inner/outer sphere boundaries, distortion, uniform drift and vortex motion. The random generator and integration are preview substitutes. Trails A ribbon from cached attachment motion, with start/end width, lifetime and fade. Spline interpolation, trail ramps and distortion are not reproduced. Audio Overlapping cues, sound-set loops and pitch variation, and effect volume curves. Spatial falloff and changing pitch during a cue are not reproduced. Persistent locator effects Named source-bone attachments and fade events. The special Health Bar and Projectile Spawn source slots use model locators; when several match, the preview uses the first. Advanced source/target links still need an engine comparison. Terrain decals A subdivided surface follows the cached scene terrain. Static decals can also project onto stationary model surfaces. Projection and shading remain approximations of the game. Water decals Animated 3D DDS texture slices follow the effect's animation-time curve. Placement uses a flat water surface; scene waves, fog and shadow variants are not reproduced. Physics pieces Cached falling, force, mass, torque and collision motion. Box-based inertia/contact proxies substitute for the game's collision shapes and solver. Physics groups and point forces Ground offsets, within-group collisions, and attraction/repulsion through range and power curves. Legacy wind Force nodes Retained in the resource report; they do not drive the preview simulation yet. Camera shake Reported without moving the artist's camera.

Additive, screen, multiply and alpha blending have separate preview paths. Premultiplied alpha and blends that depend on the already rendered background remain approximations.

Effects with glow automatically receive a separate render pass and Blender bloom. No extra artist controls are needed. The preview copies your compositor and restores the original when cleared; a replacement you select yourself is kept. Set up your render before clicking Update Preview. Blender's bloom shape and brightness differ from the game, so check the final glow in the Map Editor.

Water volume textures are decoded when the preview is built. Playback and scrubbing reuse cached slices. Large volumes use fewer slices to bound memory; the report lists this reduction. Ordinary 2D water textures use a static fallback. Water lighting is approximate.

To preview terrain contacts, place a terrain mesh outside the model's export collection, then click Update Preview. The preview snapshots visible environment meshes without changing them. Without an environment surface, physics and terrain decals use a flat ground plane at the model origin. Static decals can project onto stationary model surfaces; animated figures are excluded to prevent stretched projections. Rebuild after changing the environment geometry.

Physics uses the traced default gravity and force scaling, but its box inertia and collision response differ from the game. Check final contacts, stacking, advanced links and unsupported shader behavior in the Map Editor. Continue editing the effect itself in the external Effect Editor; the Blender tools edit the model's EffectSet references and timing.

SFP particles, trails, force fields and physics cache motion when you click Update Preview. Rebuild after changing the model animation. Playback and scrubbing reuse that cache. Unchanged decal projections are reused too. Long clips or large particle systems use reduced sampling to keep memory use bounded. A model preview is capped at 8,192 particle sprites and 64 simulated debris pieces; the report tells you when a limit reduces the preview.

SFP flames that produce no glow use smooth transparency automatically. Emitters that produce glow keep the separate glow pass. These choices come from the effect data and need no artist controls. Rebuild older previews after updating the add-on.

For refraction meshes inside effects, click Update Preview, use Add Render if your model has no camera or lights, then press F12. The render automatically uses the refraction texture to distort the background, including the effect's animated fade. The normal viewport still uses a simpler glass-like shader. A visible background makes the distortion easier to judge. The extra render passes take more render time and are removed with Clear Preview; the previous compositor is preserved. Only the frontmost distortion surface is sampled, and the texture's blur/mip control is not reproduced. Compare overlapping haze and final lighting with the Map Editor.

Check Effect Preview Report in Blender's Text Editor for the selected assets' limits. Always test the exported result in the Map Editor; the Blender preview is not yet a visual match for every effect type.

A successful inspection confirms that the file can be read. It does not prove that every dependency is installed or that the effect will attach correctly in game.

docs.title: 4. Export and Test
docs.text:
1. Save EffectSet and AnimationSet changes, then save the .blend.
  2. Export the model and its required SKA clips. An EffectSet reference alone does not export its SKA; add the appropriate AnimationSet mapping or export that clip separately.
  3. Install any custom effect, texture and sound assets separately. The DRS stores references; it does not bundle them.
  4. Reimport a copy of the export and check its entries. Then test it in the Map Editor.

docs.title: Common Problems
docs.text:
Problem Check No effect visible in Blender Click Update Preview, check the resource paths and current animation time, then read Effect Preview Report for missing dependencies or unsupported components. Resource not found Check the library folders and filename. A sound may reference an XML sound set or require an SNR/SNS pair. Resource name is ambiguous Use a unique resource name or remove duplicate test assets from your configured library. Event happens at the wrong pose Time is a fraction of the entire clip, not seconds or a frame number. Only one animation variant has an effect Add entries for each SKA clip that needs the event. Fade does nothing Confirm that an existing persistent locator effect uses that resource name.

For animation mappings, see the Advanced Abilities Guide. For effect attachment points, see the Advanced Locators Guide.

docs.title: Locator Editor
docs.text: Locators are attachment points for effects, projectiles, health bars and model parts.

docs.title: Edit a locator
docs.text:
1. Select your model and open DRS Editor → Locator Editor.
  2. Select a locator in the list, or click + beside the list and choose its type.
  3. Choose Attach to. For a resource locator, select its Effect or Resource.
  4. Click Apply Changes.
  5. Move or rotate the marker in the viewport, then click Save Placement.
  6. Save your .blend and export the model.

The list stays short; scroll to see more entries. − beside the list removes the selected locator record and its marker. Only relevant fields appear below the list. Hover over Attach to for a description of each choice.

Changing an attachment starts the locator at its new attachment's origin. Changing only its type or filename keeps its placement. Apply pending detail edits before saving placement.

docs.title: Choose an attachment
docs.text:
Choice What it means Model Moves with the model, without following a particular bone. Skeleton Gives the effect access to the model's skeleton, so the effect can use its own bone links. Bone Follows the bone you choose.

For imported models, keep the original attachment unless you intend to change it. Skeleton does not mean the first or root bone. Firedancer uses it for one persistent effect whose internal emitters attach to her head and hands.

The old checkbox stored Model as -1 and Skeleton as -2. These are real engine attachment modes. The new names replace the numeric checkbox; imported values are preserved.

docs.title: Choose and preview an effect
docs.text:
1. Configure Skylords Reborn Folder in the add-on preferences. See the Effects Guide.
  2. Select a Persistent Figure FX or Persistent Building FX locator.
  3. Click the search icon beside Effect to open Effect Selector. Search by name or choose a category.
  4. Preview auditions the resource. Use Resource updates the draft filename; Cancel keeps the previous one.
  5. Click Apply Changes, then Update Preview. Press Space to play the timeline.

Audio and Live Update sit below the preview button. Live Update refreshes resource edits after you pause editing. × beside Update Preview clears the model's generated FX and audio. State-triggered effects require the corresponding game state; they are not automatically played as persistent effects.

Firedancer's Idle fire comes from her persistent locator, not an Idle EffectSet entry. It can play without an animation event.

Categories are filename hints. The source effect files remain external assets; assigning a reference does not copy them into the DRS. Create or edit effects in the external Effect Editor.

docs.title: Placement and export
docs.text:
• Use +, rather than duplicating marker objects. Duplicated markers can share the same internal identity.
  • Use Save Placement after moving or rotating markers. Export uses saved locator data, not unsaved viewport movement.
  • Deleting a marker alone does not remove its saved locator. Use − beside the list.
  • Module references can show imported model parts. Changing a filename does not automatically rebuild construction geometry.
  • Preserve imported unknown types. IDs 14 and 15 are not offered for new locators.
  • Test attachments through representative animations and in the Map Editor after export.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Problem Check No locator list Select a mesh or collection belonging to the intended model. A bone attachment cannot be selected Import the model's skeleton first. A marker moves to the origin Changing attachment resets placement. Position it afterward and Save Placement. A locator returns after deleting its marker Remove the record with − beside the list. Export uses an old position Save Placement before exporting. The effect is missing Check the library path and resource filename, then Update Preview. Game-state FX may require their activation state.

See the Effects Guide for animation-triggered effects and sounds, and the Unit Creation Guide for the full workflow.

docs.title: Advanced Shading Guide
docs.text: For the current Blender 5 material system, use the Artist Material Workflow. This page is a practical overview; this guide covers extra painting and shading tasks and preview limits.

docs.title: 1. Start with the DRS material layout
docs.text: Select the render mesh and open DRS Editor > Material Editor. Choose Create / Upgrade DRS Material when needed. An upgrade creates a new material; keep the previous version until you have checked the result. Choose the appropriate engine material handler and assign its textures and parameters. An arbitrary Blender node graph is not baked into a game shader.

docs.title: 2. Texture suffixes and channels
docs.text:
For inspected Default variants, the parameter map uses R smoothness, G metalness, B flow mask or reflection input depending on the shader variant, and A emissivity. The same texture identifier has other meanings in legacy specular handlers, so use the selected material type rather than guessing from a filename. Color-map opacity is separate from parameter-map alpha.

When using separate artist maps, the current packer converts roughness to 1 - roughness for R, writes metalness to G, the flow/reflection input to B and emissivity to A. Use matching dimensions; missing separate maps fall back to the packed map or zero.

docs.title: 3. Material flags: supported controls versus unknowns
docs.text: Flag labels depend on the material handler; a bit does not necessarily have a universal meaning. Calculate Map Flags or Auto map flags calculates the Default material's parameter and normal map bits from enabled images while retaining other bits. Preserve unknown imported flags unless you have a reason to change them. Review the resulting material in the game.

docs.title: 4. Normal maps
docs.text: Assign the normal image to its supported texture slot and enable the appropriate flag. Treat it as non-color data. The exporter calculates geometry tangents from the active UV layer; check UV seams and compare a fresh import.

docs.title: 5. Refraction and environment cubemaps
docs.text:
Default refraction uses a refraction texture, color and scale. For the inspected shader, RG shifts a screen-color sample, B influences mip bias and alpha contributes the filtered background. The camera compositor reproduces part of this behavior; its B-channel blur, render ordering, lighting and edge behavior are incomplete. Viewport refraction is a separate approximation. Refraction does not automatically enable an environment-map flag. Validate this effect in the Map Editor.

Environment map handling also varies by material; Blender's environment response is an approximation of the game's renderer. Test it with the intended game resources.

docs.title: 6. Flow animation
docs.text:
Assign a fluid map and parameter map, adjust the Default Flow controls, and play or scrub the timeline. Parameter-map B is the flow mask in the inspected flow shader. The preview uses recovered turbulence math and a deterministic animation sequence; game random history, texture format, shading coordinates and lighting can differ. Write Flow controls whether the named flow vectors are serialized, not whether the presence of a fluid map selects the game shader's flow path. Use the Custom Flow Settings controls to change movement.

Flow uses the mesh's rest positions and advances while the timeline plays. Moving a bone should not drag the procedural fluid pattern through the surface; keeping the body still should not stop the flow. The plugin supplies the rest-position attribute automatically and upgrades older flow graphs when the timeline advances.

During playback, flow continues when the SKA animation loops. Pausing holds the fluid; pressing Space again resumes it. Changing clips or clip FPS does not restart its motion. Scrubbing while paused sets the fluid to that timeline time. Renders use timeline time too, so rendering the same frame gives the same fluid pattern. This can differ from the continuously running viewport after several clip loops.

The preview integrates flow at a fixed 60 updates per second. This is a repeatable Blender preview policy; the game's shared random state and rendering history can still produce a different pattern.

docs.title: 7. Wind
docs.text: In Default Material Parameters, enable WindResponse and WindHeight. The preview modifier is managed automatically. Play the timeline to see the movement. The engine uses height along local game Y and a world-space wind displacement. The preview follows the default engine wind field; individual maps can supply different wind. Wind pauses while painting and resumes when leaving Texture Paint.

docs.title: 8. Export and verification checklist
docs.text:
• Use the correct active material and UV layer for each exported mesh. Confirm enabled images are present.
  • Export to a separate folder, then inspect the DRS and DDS files and any referenced resources.
  • Reimport the exported model into a fresh scene and compare the material and mesh.
  • Check animations, wind, flow, refraction, alpha edges and lighting in the Map Editor or game. Blender preview is not a pixel-match guarantee.

For supported and unresolved material families, raw records and texture conversion, see the Artist Material Workflow. For the complete model workflow, start with the Artist Model Pipeline.

docs.title: Soft transparency for a simple surface
docs.text:
For a simple transparent mesh, try SimpleTextured. Assign its Texture with a grayscale opacity gradient in the image alpha channel: white is visible, black is transparent, and gray gives partial visibility. Start with white Color, material Alpha 1, and UseVertexColor disabled. Lower material Alpha for an additional fade across the whole surface. Use a texture format that retains alpha.

Alpha Test is a cutout operation and does not enable smooth transparency by itself. Do not put the opacity gradient in Default's ParamMap alpha; that channel controls emissivity.

If transparent surfaces overlap incorrectly, try DisableDepthWrite while keeping depth testing enabled, and check the result in the Map Editor. Changing to SimpleTextured also changes the shader: it does not preserve Default's normal/PAR lighting or FluidMap flow. Test a flowing waterfall separately before replacing its existing material. This recipe is supported by engine/shader analysis; it has not been visually checked on every model.

docs.title: Keep flow on a soft-edged waterfall
docs.text:
If a waterfall already uses Default's FluidMap, keep that material for the first test. The game supports flow together with its refraction screen lookup. Start with RefractionScale 0, a white RefractionColor, and a refraction map with neutral RG and black B. This brings in the background without adding distortion or an extra blur bias.

For a soft bottom edge, reduce the water contribution while increasing the background contribution in the same area. Refraction-map alpha adds background; it does not automatically fade out the water. Use the ParamMap blue flow mask to fade flow locally, and make sure the underlying ColorMap and any glow or highlights do not leave a solid edge. Disable Alpha Test for this test.

A readable moving body with a fade near the bottom is a useful starting point. Only add subtle distortion after the edge works. Review the actual model in the Map Editor: this setup follows the engine shader, but a finished visual match depends on the model's existing textures and lighting.

docs.title: Building Creation Guide
docs.text:
Buildings add a mesh grid, mesh states, and referenced resources to the ordinary DRS mesh/material workflow. A .bmg is not simply a static .drs with a different filename.

Start with the Object Creation Guide for mesh, material, collision, and GO basics. Use the Unit Creation Guide for skeletons and SKA actions when the building is animated.

Current support: Blender 5 can export new static buildings and edited imported buildings, including skinned state resources and SKA actions. Export rebuilds hidden states too, preserves source metadata, and validates output in a temporary folder. New output still needs Map Editor/in-game validation. Debris XML and construction BMS graphs remain separate authoring work; their preview meshes are not rebuilt automatically.

For skinned states, export operates on temporary mesh copies, ignores non-bone modifier groups, keeps the strongest four bone weights and normalizes them. Unweighted vertices stop a building-state export; assign appropriate deform weights and retry. Warnings about coincident positions with different weights need review as described in the Unit Creation Guide.

To start a new static building, select its render meshes in Object Mode and choose N > BMG Editor > Building Authoring & Export > Building from Selected Meshes. This moves them into the central cell's undamaged S0 state. Use Create / Upgrade Selected Material for ordinary Blender materials, then configure the DRS material controls. New skinned buildings should start from a compatible animated BMG so the skeleton, animations and state relationships are available.

docs.title: 1. Start from an Existing Building
docs.text:
For building work, importing a comparable building is more useful than starting with an empty object scene. It supplies the mesh-state relationships, resource names, and grid metadata that the simple scene generator does not create.

  1. Keep the source .bmg, its referenced state .drs files, textures, debris XML, and any .ska files together in their expected resource layout.
  2. Choose File > Import > Battleforge (.drs/.bmg) and select the building.
  3. Review the import options before confirming. Clear Scene is on by default; disable it if you need to keep the current scene.
  4. Save the imported setup to a new .blend file before editing it.

Useful options:

Option Purpose Apply Transform Controls the import's GO display-axis conversion. Use the same setting when comparing two imports. Import Collision Shape Imports building-level collision and eligible state collision data. Import S0 Collision Shapes Also imports collision from undamaged state DRS files; off by default because building-level collision can already represent those states. Import Debris Imports the referenced debris setup where available. Import Construction Imports referenced construction pieces. Import Animation Enables animation import for a rigged building.

A missing referenced file is a resource problem, not something that can be fixed by changing a collection's name.

docs.title: 2. Understand the Imported Structure
docs.text:
A typical imported building contains the following collection structure. Optional resources and Blender numeric suffixes vary by asset:

Text Only
DRSModel_<building>
├── GameOrientation                  (Empty object)
├── GroundDecal_Collection            (optional)
├── CollisionShapes_Collection        (building-level collision, if present)
│   ├── Boxes_Collection
│   ├── Spheres_Collection
│   └── Cylinders_Collection
├── Armature_Collection              (if the building is rigged)
├── SLocators_Collection              (construction helpers, if imported)
└── MeshSetGrid_0
    ├── MeshSet_0
    │   ├── Active_State_MeshSet_0    (Empty marker)
    │   └── States_Collection_0
    │       ├── S0_Undamaged
    │       │   └── Meshes_Collection
    │       ├── S2_Damaged
    │       │   ├── Meshes_Collection
    │       │   └── CollisionShapes_Collection (when imported)
    │       └── Debris_Collection
    │           ├── S2_Debris
    │           └── S3_Debris
    └── MeshSet_1 ...

A state can contain its own collision subcollections. The grid references individual mesh sets, and each mesh set groups its related states. Do not flatten all state meshes into the root or combine every state into one ordinary object export collection.

docs.title: GO and parenting
docs.text:
Good practice: Use the building's GO coordinate convention consistently for new meshes, collision shapes, and non-bone helpers. Parenting a new primitive before fitting it is convenient, but not a required modeling order; correcting and applying a mesh rotation after parenting is also a supported workflow.

Collection nesting is not object parenting. Inspect the actual parent relationship when adding a mesh to an imported state. Keep existing armature and bone-attached relationships intact rather than parenting every object directly to GO. Do not reset or apply GO itself to compensate for one misaligned state.

The mesh-grid visualization expects the model's GO helper to exist. Keeping that helper for the editor is different from requiring every mesh to be parented before modeling.

docs.title: 3. Inspect States in the BMG Editor
docs.text:
Open the 3D Viewport sidebar (N) and select BMG Editor > BMG State Editor.

Button What to inspect Show undamaged The S0_Undamaged meshes. Show damaged The S2_Damaged meshes on their own. Show damaged + Debris (should look undamaged) Damaged geometry together with S2_Debris; useful for checking how pieces fit. Show Debris The imported debris collections. Show All Stages All state collections together for comparison. Overlapping geometry is expected in this view.

These controls switch visibility; they do not create missing states, author debris physics, or define gameplay transitions. The Switch All States controls operate on mesh sets across the scene, so take care when several buildings are loaded.

Use Show Collision Shapes and Show SLocators to reduce clutter. Hiding a helper for editing is not a substitute for removing unwanted resource references from an export setup.

docs.title: 4. Inspect or Fit a Mesh Grid
docs.text:
Make the intended DRSModel_... root active before using the grid controls.

  • Show Mesh Grid toggles the visualization.
  • Create Grid fits new grid metadata to eligible undamaged-state meshes. It uses a fixed cell size of 2.0 and currently creates a square grid with an odd number of cells along each axis.
  • Rotation changes the editor's grid/model orientation in degrees. It is not a reason to rotate GO manually.
  • Center Pivot At Origin (0,0,0) chooses whether the grid is centered at the origin or the detected model center.
  • Remove Grid removes stored grid data and its visualization, not the building's visible meshes.

Save before recreating a grid. Create Grid rebuilds metadata and resets the grid/model rotation to zero before fitting; it is not a harmless visibility toggle. Review the result instead of assuming an imported layout or cell assignment was preserved.

The fitting code looks for meshes inside the undamaged-state Meshes_Collection hierarchy. An ordinary object scene with no S0_Undamaged meshes is not automatically a fully configured building just because the grid button is available. Empty or unexpectedly small grids are a reason to check the hierarchy and dimensions first.

A visible grid is an authoring aid, not proof that the complete BMG state graph can currently be exported.

docs.title: 5. Edit Materials, Collision, and Optional Resources
Visible meshes and materials
docs.text: Edit each state's render meshes in its own Meshes_Collection. Apply the same UV, triangulation, material, and vertex-budget checks described in the Object Creation Guide. Use the Advanced Shading Guide for packed parameters, wind, refraction, and environment maps.

docs.title: Collision
docs.text:
Keep building-level collision separate from damage-state collision. A damaged state may need a different approximation than the undamaged building.

When adding a shape, use its state's matching box/sphere/cylinder collection. As for visible meshes, using the correct model's GO is good practice; fitting the shape first and correcting its rotation after parenting is also possible. Preserve the primitive's geometry: boxes remain rectangular, spheres remain round, and cylinders remain circular and capped. See Object Creation Guide, step 8.

docs.title: Ground decal
docs.text: GroundDecal_Collection is imported when the BMG references a ground decal DRS. It is optional and distinct from both building collision and the grid visualization. Its render meshes are rebuilt into <building>_ground.drs; the BMG reference and textures are updated automatically.

docs.title: Construction pieces and debris
docs.text: Preserve their referenced assets and imported relationships. A construction helper or debris mesh is not equivalent to a finished building state. Export preserves their references and copies locally resolvable dependencies, but does not replace an external debris/resource authoring workflow.

docs.title: 6. Animated Buildings and Visual Hooks
docs.text:
Use the building's deform skeleton, skin weights, and SKA actions as described in the Unit Creation Guide. A building is not limited to one idle animation: relevant assets may use spawn, attack, casting, channeling, or turret-related animation modes.

Choose only the modes required by the target asset. A long list of available animation types is not a checklist that every building needs to implement. See the Advanced Abilities Guide for action/marker relationships and the Advanced Effects Guide for sound metadata.

Non-bone locators use the model's coordinate convention, while bone locators follow the armature. Use the Advanced Locators Guide rather than manually forcing all helpers under GO.

docs.title: 7. Author States and Grid Settings
docs.text:
Open N > BMG Editor > Building Authoring & Export. Selecting a mesh or nested state collection identifies its building; the Outliner does not need to be focused on the root.

Control Behavior Building Grid Settings Edit name, square half extent, spacing, yaw, pivot mode, ground resource and building effects. State from Selected Meshes Copy selected render meshes into the chosen cell and state ID. Common IDs are 0 intact and 2 damaged. Show Display one state for that cell, including custom numeric state IDs. Effects Edit persistent state FX and the effect triggered on entering that state. X beside a state Remove that state from the exported grid and unlink its meshes from the building. Transition effects are separate records and are retained. Export Building Package Rebuild the BMG, editable state DRS resources, ground decal and textures.

Grid half extent 1 means 3 x 3 cells, 2 means 5 x 5, and so on. Resizing preserves cell coordinates around the origin and updates state collection indices. Shrinking across a populated cell is rejected. Grid display yaw is removed from state geometry during export and written once in MeshSetGrid. Preview rotation preserves artist object transforms.

Each render mesh needs a UV map and a material. Multiple material slots become separate CDsp mesh records. Triangulation and UV/normal discontinuity splitting run on temporary copies. The engine's vertex budget still applies after splitting. Apply modeling modifiers before export; the add-on's WindEffect preview and Armature modifier are handled separately. Material types, flags, textures and parameter lists use the ordinary DRS workflow; Default flow still uses the parameter map's B channel as its mask.

Keep each cell's state IDs unique. State IDs and cell indices are collection properties, independent of Blender's automatic numeric name suffixes. Deleting a collection does not necessarily delete its preserved source record: source-only records intentionally survive. Removing source-only records requires an explicit metadata edit.

docs.title: Preview Damage and Destruction
docs.text:
1. Set your Skylords Reborn Folder in the add-on preferences.
  2. Select the building and open BMG Editor → Building Editor.
  3. Click Build Damage Preview, then drag Damage from 0% to 100%.
  4. Press Space to see debris fall and effects play. Replay Transition restarts them at the current frame.

Damage changes cell meshes, their state effects and transition effects, and the building's scratch shading. At 100%, the preview selects the destroyed state and plays the building crush effect. A destroyed state can have no replacement mesh: the falling debris is a separate effect.

Assets and physics are cached when you build the preview. Dragging Damage or scrubbing does not reload them. Use Update Damage Preview after changing geometry, materials, state effects or terrain. If playing near the end of your timeline, extend its end frame to leave time for the effect.

This is a preview control, not an exported health setting. Clear Damage Preview restores the original materials and visibility. Manual Show state controls also clear the damage preview. After reopening a saved preview, rebuild it to animate, or clear it to return to editing.

Scratch needs a scratch map with useful alpha; a white alpha mask causes no visible darkening. Buildings with several cells are damaged in a repeatable cell order. In game, the impact position changes that order. Native default inverse inertia is supported; collision/integration and engine-generated impact/crush impulses remain incomplete. Building damage preview audio is currently disabled. Create or change destruction effects in the external Effect Editor; assign their filenames through State Effects or Building Grid Settings.

The preview automatically raises Cycles' transparency depth for overlapping smoke sprites. Clearing it restores the previous value, unless you changed it yourself. This prevents black rectangles caused by the renderer ending transparent rays too early; you do not need to change the smoke textures or alpha threshold.

docs.title: 8. Export and Validate
docs.text:
1. Save the edited .blend as the working copy. Re-import buildings with this version to capture the new state/container snapshots.
  2. Choose an output folder outside the unpacked source assets. Source game files remain read only.
  3. Keep Model Type: Preserve / Auto for imported buildings. It keeps their node layout, including unknown chunks. Explicit layouts cannot discard source nodes silently.
  4. Enable Export All SKA Actions for edited animations. Prefix options update AnimationSet and EffectSet only for actions actually written. Referenced source SKAs remain dependencies when animations were not imported or exported.
  5. Inspect <building>.bmg-export.json. external_references lists references not copied into the package; these may be installed-game construction/FX resources or missing assets. Review this list before sharing the export.
  6. Re-import into a separate scene. Check S0/S2, ground decal, materials, animation references and building/state collision independently. Then verify placement, damage transitions, construction and playback in the Skylords Map Editor/in game.

Output contains <building>.bmg, <building>_cellNNN_sID.drs, optional <building>_ground.drs, DDS textures, available SKAs and local dependencies. This is an asset package for the installed game. It does not create a new database entity or a standalone map.

Validation failure leaves previous output files intact. Temporary objects/meshes/collections are removed without globally purging the artist's unused data blocks. Imported collision data stays preserved when collision import was disabled; editing loaded shapes regenerates that payload in game coordinates.

Remaining preview boundary: metadata preserves the engine's cell rotation/spacing/pivot rules, but complete viewport placement for all modular/shared-armature cases remains unfinished. Independently authoring a construction BMS or changing a debris XML graph is also outside this exporter. Automated Blender checks cover a new two-state building, Heal Well and Bandits Artillery; live engine playback remains to be checked.
