docs.title: Default Material Guide
docs.text: Use this guide to set up Default materials in Blender 5. Other material types are covered in the advanced reference.

docs.title: 1. Open the Material Editor
docs.text:
1. Select the part of your model you want to edit.
  2. In the 3D Viewport, press N and open DRS Editor > Material Editor.
  3. If needed, click Create DRS Material or Create / Upgrade DRS Material.
  4. Set Material Type to Default. Stay in Artist View.

An imported model usually already has its material. Upgrading an older setup creates a new material and keeps the old one. Check the textures afterward.

docs.title: 2. Add your textures
docs.text:
Open Textures. Assign each image to its matching slot and tick the box beside it to include it. You do not need to connect shader nodes or change image settings.

Slot What to put here ColorMap The model's color texture, usually named _col. Start here. NormalMap Surface detail such as cracks and bumps, usually _nor. ParamMap A packed texture controlling surface properties, usually _par. FluidMap The moving color layer for effects such as lava, usually _flu. EnvironmentMap A reflection cubemap. Optional; see reflections below. RefractionParamMap A distortion texture for the view behind the model. Optional. ScratchMap A texture whose alpha controls the scratch darkening effect. Optional.

Leave unused maps disabled. For imported models, keep the original slot assignments; filenames alone do not decide how the game uses a texture.

Enable Auto map flags to keep the normal and parameter-map switches in sync with your assigned maps. Calculate Map Flags updates them once instead. Neither button chooses transparency or reflection settings for you.

docs.title: Choose where surface values come from
docs.text:
Use Parameter Source in Textures:

Choice Use it when… Packed _par / _spec You already have a packed parameter texture. For Default, assign it to ParamMap. Separate artist maps You have separate roughness, metalness, mask and emission images. The plugin packs them on export. Use matching image sizes. Scalar values You want one value across the whole mesh. Edit the sliders in Material Parameters.

For a Default parameter texture, the channels are:

Channel Controls Red Smoothness: higher values make smoother highlights. Green Metalness: higher values make the surface more metallic. Blue The flow mask. In reflection variants it also controls reflection contribution. Alpha Emissivity: the surface's glow contribution. This is not transparency.

In Separate artist maps mode, roughness is converted to smoothness automatically. Use grayscale images; the plugin reads each image's red channel. Missing separate maps fall back to the packed map, or zero if none is assigned.

Why did the sliders disappear? A parameter map replaces Smoothness, Metalness, Reflectivity and Emissivity. Edit the map instead. Choose Scalar values if you want to use those sliders.

docs.title: Paint a texture
docs.text:
Click Paint beside the texture slot you want to edit. The plugin creates an editable, packed working image, keeps any existing strokes, and selects it for both image and model painting. Original game files stay unchanged. Reusing Paint continues on the same working image. Edited textures are converted back to DDS when you export the model.

Some compressed DDS images can show painted pixels in the Image Editor while the model still displays old GPU texture data. Paint avoids that path by using an uncompressed working image. After painting, save your image to a separate PNG with Image > Save As, and save your .blend file.

Imported UVs may sit a whole tile below the base image. This comes from the V-axis conversion and looks the same with Repeat sampling. Paint shows one image and leaves the UVs unchanged. UVs below the base tile can remain outside the visible image; this does not change Repeat sampling on the model. Shared or overlapping UVs make a brush stroke appear on every mesh part using those pixels. For unique painting on each part, give it unique UV space and texture content first.

docs.title: 3. Enable the features you need
docs.text:
Open Material Flags. Leave imported flags alone unless you are changing that feature.

Setting When to use it UseParameterMap Use the packed or separate parameter maps. Auto map flags can handle this. UseNormalMap Use your NormalMap. Auto map flags can handle this. EnableAlphaTest Cut holes in a surface, such as the spaces between leaves. Pixels below the alpha cutoff are discarded. This does not enable smooth, glass-like transparency. UseEnvironmentMap Add reflections from a cubemap. DecalMode Use the game's decal rendering path. Leave it off for ordinary solid models.

For cutouts, put the opacity mask in ColorMap alpha. Keep ParamMap alpha for emissivity. The game's final transparency also depends on its rendering setup; check the edges in the Map Editor.

docs.title: 4. Adjust the appearance
docs.text:
Open Material Parameters and enable the values you want to export. Only controls relevant to your setup appear in Artist View. Numeric sliders stop at the supported minimum and maximum; you do not need to manage range warnings.

  • Saturation: lower it to reduce color intensity.
  • SpecularScale (approx.): adjusts highlight strength. Blender previews an approximation, so check the final result in the Map Editor.
  • Scratch: controls darkening from ScratchMap alpha. It needs a ScratchMap.
  • Smoothness, Metalness, Reflectivity, Emissivity: available in Scalar values mode. With maps enabled, edit the corresponding map channels instead.

docs.title: Moving textures: flow
docs.text:
Assign FluidMap and a parameter map with a blue flow mask. Blue marks where the fluid layer blends into the base color. Press Space to play the timeline; the mesh itself does not have to move.

To adjust the movement, open Flow — Speed and Direction and enable Custom Flow Settings:

  • Minimum Speed / Maximum Speed: the direction and speed range on each axis. Use the same minimum and maximum for steady movement.
  • Speed Variation: how the speed changes within that range.
  • Pattern Scale: the size of the flow pattern.

Leave Custom Flow Settings off to use the engine defaults. This does not disable flow.

docs.title: Bending in the wind
docs.text: In Material Parameters, enable WindResponse and WindHeight. Start with a small WindResponse within 0–0.1; zero means no movement. WindHeight (0–10) sets where bending begins along the model's game height axis. Increase it to keep more of the base still. The plugin adds the preview automatically. Press Space to see it. During Texture Paint, wind deformation is paused to keep the surface stable; it returns when you leave paint mode. Exported wind values are unchanged.

docs.title: Reflections and refraction
docs.text:
For reflections, enable UseEnvironmentMap. Assign an EnvironmentMap in Textures, or use Use Bundled Environment when that helper is shown. The game can use a fallback environment when no map is assigned.

For refraction, assign RefractionParamMap, then adjust RefractionScale and RefractionColor. The preview is set up automatically. Refraction distorts the view behind the surface; it is separate from reflections and alpha cutouts. Blender approximates this effect and does not reproduce the game's refraction blur. See refraction details only if you need to author the texture channels yourself.

docs.title: 5. Check the whole model
docs.text:
Open DRS Editor > Render Setup and click Add Render. This adds lights, a camera and a ground setup around the whole model in your current scene. The setup includes a Sun (Warm daylight), a sky fill light and a world background. Switch the viewport shading to Rendered. Press Space for flow and wind.

Exposure in Render Setup adjusts overall brightness. The default is 0; 1 makes the whole image twice as bright, including glowing textures. It does not add a missing light. For stronger directional light, adjust the Sun's Energy in Blender's Light Data Properties.

Example Blender preview. The Map Editor remains the final check for game lighting and effects.

Export a test, import it again, and check it in the Map Editor before sharing it.

docs.title: If something looks wrong
docs.text:
Problem Check first No material controls Select a mesh with an active DRS material. Texture has no effect Check the slot checkbox and its matching material flag. Smoothness or metalness sliders have no effect The parameter map may be supplying those values instead. Flow or wind is still Play the timeline with Space. Check the map or WindResponse. Rendered view is dark Use Add Render to add lighting. Blender and game look different Compare in the Map Editor; lighting, reflections and refraction have preview limits.

Need raw records, channel evidence or export-only parameters? Open the advanced material reference. You do not need Debug View for the normal workflow.

docs.title: Artist model pipeline
docs.text: This is the starting point for making or editing Skylords Reborn assets with SR-ImpEx in Blender 5. The plugin exports game data and supplies previews for some of it; the Map Editor and game are still needed to validate runtime behavior. Save a working .blend, keep original game files untouched, and export to a separate folder.

docs.title: 1. Choose the asset and starting point
docs.text:
Your goal Start here Output to check Static decoration or object Object Creation Guide DRS, texture files and any intended collision Animated unit or rigged prop Unit Creation Guide DRS, referenced SKA clips and textures Building with damage states Building Creation Guide BMG, state DRS files, textures and referenced resources Create or edit a standalone state-resource set Choose New BMS or Open under BMG Editor > BMS State Resources A BMS copy and its separately exported DRS/FX dependencies

For an existing asset, import a comparable DRS or BMG with its resources in place. Review the import dialog: Clear Scene can remove the current scene. Save a copy before editing. For a new asset, use the scene or building setup in the guide for that asset. The named collections select export contents; parenting controls transforms. Inspect both when arranging a model.

docs.title: 2. Model, rig and animate
docs.text:
1. Put render meshes in the expected Meshes_Collection, create an active UV layer, and use a separate mesh for each intended exported material. Geometry, bounds, tangents and stream counts are generated on export.
  2. For a rigged asset, use a deform armature and matching vertex groups. Review skinning with no more than four influences per vertex. Test poses throughout every clip, not just the rest pose. Select the skinned meshes in Object Mode and use DRS Editor > Animation Set Editor > Skinning > Check Skin Weights for a non-destructive summary before export.
  3. Create actions on the deform rig. Use DRS Editor > Animation Set Editor to select an animation and edit its clip FPS, duration, loop and interpolation. Confirm the clip settings, then play or scrub to inspect motion. If a control rig, IK or constraints drive it, prepare keyed deform actions on a copy and verify the reimport: the exporter does not automatically bake the rig.
  4. Configure and Save AnimationSet and EffectSet edits, and Sync from Scene after placing locator helpers. These are separate from Blender action keys. Referenced SKA clips must be included on export.

The selected clip's advanced settings can edit text markers and target IDs. The importer also preserves tracks whose bones are absent from the current skeleton. Event dispatch, target/morph mapping and the special alpha track are not simulated as game behavior in Blender. See the Advanced Abilities Guide before changing these advanced fields.

docs.title: 3. Set up materials and inspect the model
docs.text:
Select a render mesh and use DRS Editor > Material Editor to create or upgrade its material and choose a handler. Assign the enabled maps and review the flags. For the inspected Default material, parameter-map channels are R smoothness, G metalness, B flow mask or reflection input depending on the shader variant, and A emissivity. Other material handlers may use different texture roles. Do not infer a map's meaning from its filename alone. The material workflow covers separate maps, automatic flag calculation, texture conversion and all current limits.

For a compatible static Textured or SimpleTextured mesh, Create SR Vertex Colors adds an editable SR Color0 point attribute and enables the material's vertex-color flag. Imported single-stream 0x28001 meshes retain their color bytes. This stream has no normals; skinned and multi-stream variants remain unsupported. Check the RGB interpretation in the Map Editor.

For a flow material, assign the relevant maps and parameters and play or scrub the timeline to see the preview change. The timeline must advance; a paused frame remains still. For a complete render setup in the current scene, select a model mesh and click DRS Editor > Render Setup > Add Render. Its Render collection supplies camera, lights, ground and world settings for the whole visible model. For a camera refraction comparison, select the model meshes and create a scene using DRS Editor > Render Setup. After changing refracting objects, use Refresh Screen Refraction Preview and render from the preview camera. This is a controlled approximation: the engine's B-channel refraction blur, lighting and render ordering are not fully recreated. Verify both effects in the Map Editor.

docs.title: 4. Add nonvisual resources and export
docs.text:
Add collision primitives only when appropriate for the export type, fit them in Blender, then reimport and inspect their placement. Collision shapes do not by themselves establish walkable bridges or gameplay rules. Place locators for the roles required by a comparable asset; effects, sounds, projectile and ability behavior depend on engine resources, not just helper positions.

Use the DRS export type appropriate to the target. For units, save metadata and enable export of the referenced SKA actions when needed. For buildings, use BMG Editor > Building Authoring & Export to create or edit states and export the package; inspect its dependency manifest. For standalone BMS files, the BMS panel edits references and can import a state DRS for visual editing, but the BMS export does not package that DRS or its FX automatically. Set its Resource directory and use Check State Resources to find local missing references before delivery. Engine-resolved references may need a different resource root; the check establishes local file availability only.

Unknown material records and source-only metadata can often be preserved; they do not acquire a speculative visual effect in Blender. Some resource classes and full multi-cell building preview are still incomplete. The advanced guides identifies the applicable preservation, external file-tool or editor-test path for each family. A hex/template edit should be made on a separate copy and followed by a fresh import and engine test, since arbitrary values are not automatically validated by Blender.

docs.title: 5. Validate a fresh export
docs.text:
• Export to a new folder and review reported errors, filenames and referenced DRS, SKA, DDS and FX resources. Save the .blend separately.
  • Import the exported result into a fresh scene and check geometry, UV seams, materials, weights, full animation ranges, locator positions and collision.
  • For a building, check each state and the dependency manifest. Shared-armature multi-cell placement is not fully reproduced in the current Blender preview.
  • Test the result in the Map Editor and, when appropriate, in game. Compare flow, refraction, animation events, collision and lighting against the intended behavior; a successful Blender render is not a runtime test.

docs.title: Edit an animation in one place
docs.text:
In Animation Set Editor, choose an ability and its animation variant. The selected Action owns Clip Settings: frame rate, first frame, duration, loop/clamp addressing and interpolation. OK automatically derives the clip range from its existing keys; it does not move keys. With keys present, the first frame and frame count are calculated and read-only. Without keys, the stored range remains editable. Changing FPS changes playback duration without resampling keys. Clip edits apply to this selected Action even when a different animation is currently playing. Shared Actions share these settings across all variants that reference them.

Advanced SKA Data is collapsed by default. It preserves and edits SKA text events and Target IDs, but their practical authoring and target mapping are not fully verified. Blender does not execute these engine events. These SKA events are separate from AnimationSet spawn/cast markers. Debug View additionally shows preserved tracks and version/completeness controls. Skin weight tools remain under Animation Set Editor > Skinning when a skinned mesh is selected. The separate SKA Editor panel has been removed. Restart Blender after updating.

AnimationSet Play respects the selected SKA's Loop/Clamp addressing: Loop repeats the preview range; Clamp stops at its endpoint. In Start/Loop/End previews, Loop repeats just that segment. Start, End, Cast, Resolve and marker previews play once. Space remains Blender's global timeline playback.

docs.title: Static Object: from Blender to DRS
docs.text: Export a rock, prop or other non-animated object with SR-ImpEx.

docs.title: A. Edit an existing DRS
docs.text:
1. Put the .drs and its textures in the same folder.
  2. Choose File → Import → Battleforge Model (.drs/.bmg) and open the .drs.
  3. Select the visible model mesh and make your changes.

Continue at step 3. Skip Set Up Model.

docs.title: B. Make a model from scratch
docs.text: Create your model in Blender. Select its meshes, then follow step 2.

docs.title: C. Use a model from another program
docs.text:
Import the model with Blender. Select its meshes, then follow step 2.

Using a rigged model as a static object

Duplicate the meshes and convert the copies to meshes in the desired pose. Continue with these copies.

docs.title: 2. Set up a new model
docs.text:
Skip this step for an imported DRS.

  1. Select your model meshes.
  2. Open DRS Editor → Model Setup → Set Up Model.
  3. Choose Static Object, enter a name such as object_stone_block, and keep Include Selected Meshes enabled.
  4. Leave Collision Support off for now and click OK.

GameOrientation — your model's parent object

GameOrientation keeps your model aligned with the game. Import and Set Up Model create it for you.

  • Move, rotate and resize your meshes. Leave GameOrientation unchanged.
  • Keep the meshes in Meshes_Collection and parented to this model's GameOrientation.
  • Moving a mesh into the collection does not parent it.
Advanced: add another mesh

Move the new mesh into this model's Meshes_Collection and parent it to GameOrientation using Object (Keep Transform).

Use the GameOrientation from the same model. Keep existing rigged meshes attached to their armature.

docs.title: 3. Check your model
docs.text:
• Use UV-mapped meshes with geometry modifiers applied.
  • Use one DRS material per mesh. Separate multi-material meshes by material.
  • Check size and facing against an imported game object if you have one available.

Already imported a DRS and only changed its shape? Keep its existing material and go to step 6.

Advanced: large models and export errors
  • Keep each mesh and the combined model below 32,767 exported vertices. Leave room for extra vertices at UV seams.
  • If you reach the limit, reduce the geometry or export smaller, separate DRS objects.
  • Apply geometry modifiers on a copy before exporting. Keep the editable original.
  • If export fails, read the add-on log and fix the reported object first.

docs.title: 4. Create a DRS material
docs.text: Select a mesh and open DRS Editor → Material Editor. Click Create DRS Material, or Create / Upgrade DRS Material for a mesh that already has a material. Choose Default as the material type and keep Artist View.

docs.title: 5. Load your textures
docs.text:
1. Open Textures.
  2. Click the folder icon beside ColorMap and choose your PNG or DDS color texture.
  3. If you have a normal map, load it into NormalMap.
  4. Leave Auto map flags enabled.

For an imported DRS, keep the assigned textures or replace the ones you want to change. For a foreign model, load its textures here.

Check the result in Material Preview. For a lit preview, use DRS Editor → Render Setup → Add Render.

For cut-out leaves or fences, enable EnableAlphaTest under Material Flags. See the Default Material Guide for more material options.

Optional: add simple collision shapes

Enable Collision Support in step 2 if your object needs collision.

  1. Add cubes, spheres or cylinders and fit them around your model.
  2. Move them into Boxes_Collection, Spheres_Collection or Cylinders_Collection.
  3. Parent them to GameOrientation using Object (Keep Transform).
  4. Set the collision helpers to Wire display.

Keep boxes rectangular, spheres round and cylinders circular. Avoid bevels and shear. After export, reimport with collision shapes enabled and check their fit.

docs.title: 6. Export
docs.text:
1. Select a mesh belonging to the model.
  2. Open DRS Editor → Model Setup → Export DRS.
  3. Choose a separate output folder and a filename such as object_stone_block.drs.
  4. Check Static Object (no collision), or Static Object (with collision) if appropriate.
  5. Keep Mip Maps → Auto and the other defaults. Click Export DRS.
Advanced: export options

For extra mesh controls, open Advanced Mesh Settings in the export window.

Option Setting Split Mesh by UV Islands Keep enabled unless you have prepared the splits yourself. Flip Normals Use only to correct confirmed inside-out faces. Auto-fix Quad Faces Keep enabled to export quads as triangles. Mip Maps Keep Auto. Change only to limit the exported mip levels. Keep Debug Collection Enable to inspect the prepared export copy.

docs.title: 7. Check the exported copy
docs.text:
1. Keep the exported .drs and .dds textures together in the output folder.
  2. Import the DRS into a fresh Blender scene. Check its orientation, size and textures.
  3. Test it in the Skylords Map Editor.

If a texture is missing, check its slot in Material Editor and the export folder.

docs.title: Unit Creation Guide
docs.text:
This guide walks through the basic setup for creating a unit or animated object with the SR-ImpEx Blender plugin.

First follow the shared scene, mesh, UV, and material setup in the Object Creation Guide. Do not copy the static-object collision or export choices unchanged: units and animated objects use different export types.

Target DRS export type Important difference A unit with animation/locator metadata Animated Unit Writes unit animation, effect, and locator blocks; does not export the object collision-shape block. A rigged prop or animated object Animated Object (no collision) or Animated Object (with collision) Can use simple object collision when that type is chosen. It does not gain unit locators simply by being animated. A building with states/grid resources Building export types Follow the Building Creation Guide, including its current export limitations.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
A unit or animated object needs:

  • a deform armature and its skeleton/rest pose;
  • render meshes with an Armature modifier referencing that deform armature;
  • vertex groups that match the intended deform bones, with valid skin weights;
  • Blender actions and animation metadata appropriate to the target asset.

Each vertex can use up to 4 bone influences. On the temporary export copy, the exporter excludes groups that do not match skeleton bones, keeps the four strongest bone weights and normalizes their sum. The original Blender mesh and its modifier-mask groups remain unchanged. Review export warnings: unweighted vertices are not automatically assigned a guessed bone. Check deformation after a fresh import, since limiting weights can change the result.

To check before exporting, select the skinned mesh or meshes in Object Mode and choose DRS Editor > Animation Set Editor > Skinning > Check Skin Weights. The panel reports vertices with no matching bone weights, more than four bone influences, non-normalized bone weights and non-bone groups. Non-bone groups may be intentional modifier masks; the export copy excludes them, but the inspector does not remove or modify anything. The result is a snapshot: run the check again after editing weights or changing the selection. After a check, the Unweighted, Over 4, and Unnormalized buttons select the matching vertices on the active skinned mesh and enter Edit Mode so you can locate them. These buttons replace that mesh's current vertex selection and deselect other meshes before entering Edit Mode, but do not alter weights.

The CGeo collision/query mesh welds coincident positions. If those positions have different bone weights, its skin record can keep only one weight set; the export log warns and retains the first weighted set. Make the corresponding weights agree or separate the positions, then verify collision/query behavior in the editor. Render meshes still have their own per-mesh skin streams.

The new-scene operator creates the shared object collections, not a finished character rig. Put the deform armature in a direct child collection named Armature_Collection and render meshes directly in Meshes_Collection. Start from an imported, compatible skeleton when possible; changing a skeleton/rest pose without checking the skin and animations can break their agreement.

docs.title: GO and rig relationships
docs.text:
Recommended practice: Keep the armature and meshes in one consistent model coordinate convention. When using GameOrientation (GO), leave the armature under the model's helper and keep skinned meshes attached to their deform armature. Parenting before modeling is convenient, not a required order of operations.

Do not reparent every skinned mesh directly to GO just because a static mesh can be authored that way. Bone-attached locators also stay attached to bones. Avoid applying transforms to GO, the armature, or an existing bound rig as a blanket rotation fix; changes to a rig need animation and skin validation, not just a still-frame check. See GameOrientation and adding meshes.

docs.title: 1. Set Up the Required Locators
docs.text:
A unit also uses locators.

The following are common starting points, not a universally enforced minimum set. Match the needs of a comparable working unit and its gameplay resources. Add them through DRS Editor > CDrwLocatorList with the top-level DRSModel_... collection active:

  • HealthBar: a health-bar/UI position, commonly left without a bone parent.
  • Hit: a hit-related point; bone attachment depends on the asset.
  • Projectile_Spawn: a projectile-origin position/orientation where the asset uses that role.

Adding a locator alone does not define a projectile, damage rule, or gameplay ability. The current DRS writer includes CDrwLocatorList for Animated Unit, not the animated-object export types.

Use this order to avoid losing locator placement:

  1. Add an entry or choose an existing one, then set Type, File if needed, and Parent. A bone parent makes it follow that bone; an empty parent field is a model-root point.
  2. Click Update parent and remove transformations to commit the metadata/attachment. This resets position and rotation, so do it before final placement, not after.
  3. Move and rotate the scene locator to its intended point. Scrub an animation if it is bone-attached.
  4. Make the model root active again and click Sync from Scene. This writes scene transforms/attachments into the model's saved locator data; it is not just a UI refresh.
  5. Save the .blend file. Export reads the saved locator data, not an unsynchronized scene marker.

GO note: A non-bone locator can use the model's GO convention; a bone locator must remain bone-local. The editor manages this distinction. Do not manually reparent every locator to GO or use the parent-reset button as a keep-transform operation.

See the Advanced Locators Guide for supported types, resource references, multiple-model selection, and the difference between changing metadata and syncing scene transforms.

docs.title: 2. Understand Units vs. Animated Objects
docs.text:
For the selected animation variant, DRS Editor > Animation Set Editor provides Clip Settings and playback. Text events and Target IDs are in the collapsed Advanced SKA Data section; their usage is not fully verified. Play sets the Blender scene range and frame rate automatically; OK in Clip Settings automatically fits the stored clip range to include the keyed subframes without moving keys. Review the range afterward, especially when retiming an imported action. SKA text markers are separate from the AnimationSet markers described below: neither event system is executed by the Blender preview. See the Advanced Abilities Guide.

For cubic curves, SKA has one tangent per key while Blender can use different incoming and outgoing handle slopes. Prefer aligned handles, and reimport the exported clip to check motion between keys, especially after adjusting handle lengths or using keys close together on subframes.

A unit usually has multiple animation modes. The current animated-object export path keeps the Idle visibility job and removes unit-style markers/timings; selecting Animated Object is not a way to export a unit with fewer requirements.

The editor's initialization template provides a useful starting list, not an exporter-enforced guarantee that every unit needs exactly these animations:

  • Idle
  • Walk
  • Run
  • Spawn
  • HitFromBack
  • Cheer/Emote
  • HitFromFront
  • Die
  • HitFromLeft
  • HitFromRight
  • PushBackStandUp (Loop)

Loop animations have three parts: start, loop, and end. The loop section should be the repeated part. A good example is a unit being pushed back continuously by wind and staying inside the same repeated motion.

There are more animation types available. Check the Animation Set Editor and a comparable working asset for the relevant set. Entries marked Not yet Supported, such as ModeSwitch, are not an authoring promise.

docs.title: Actions and saved metadata are separate
docs.text:
1. Create or import the Blender actions on the deform rig, then choose their references in the AnimationSet rows.
  2. Use Init → Unit to add the Idle, Walk, Run, Spawn and Die starter mappings. Existing entries are kept unless you enable Replace Existing Mappings. Assign an Action to each entry you need.
  3. Choose animation modes, variants, weights, and any markers, then click Save in the AnimationSet editor to persist them to the model collection.
  4. Save the .blend file as well. Reset reloads saved metadata; it does not save pending edits.

An action existing in Blender's Action list does not mean it is referenced by the saved AnimationSet or will be included in Export All SKA Actions.

docs.title: 3. Add Animation Variants
docs.text:
You can create multiple variants for the same animation and assign a weight to each one.

For example, if you want two idle animations and one should play most of the time, you can assign weights like this:

  • default idle: 80
  • special idle: 20

Using a total of 100 makes the intended weighting easy to review. The editor accepts individual values from 0 to 100, but does not automatically normalize or validate the total.

Other important settings:

  • Allows IK: enabled for new variants by default; metadata, not an IK-baking command.
  • Force No Blend: disabled for new variants by default; preserve deliberate imported settings.

For a unit that uses melee attacks, configure the appropriate attack mode and marker relationship required by that asset. The add-on stores the animation/visual metadata; it does not create the gameplay ability itself.

docs.title: 4. Add Markers for Important Animations
docs.text:
Some animations, especially Spawn and Attack, need a marker.

Markers store an event position and normalized point in an animation. Assets can use them for spawn, attack, and other visual/gameplay timing, but the add-on does not validate when an external gameplay system makes a unit controllable or applies a hit.

Marker Time is a fraction from 0 to 1, not seconds or a frame number. In a 5-second clip, 0.6 means 3 seconds. To target 0.6 seconds in that clip, enter 0.12.

Match the marker's animation type/visibility job to the intended mode and preview the relevant variant. Do not assume an identically named Blender action automatically creates that relationship. The editor derives timing metadata from the referenced clip and marker settings; the displayed millisecond timing fields are read-only.

Useful marker tools:

  • Display Marker: previews the animation at the selected marker time
  • Play Marker: plays the animation until the marker time so you can fine-tune the timing
  • XYZ: sets the exact 3D marker position

Place the marker where the target asset expects the event position, such as a weapon or hand attachment point. Check its displayed position against the animated pose rather than only against the rest pose.

A marker and a Projectile_Spawn locator may use related positions, but they are separate data. Moving one does not automatically update the other; save AnimationSet edits and sync locator edits through their respective editors.

For more animation types such as spell casting or ranged attacks, check the Advanced Abilities Guide.

docs.title: 5. Configure Basic Unit Settings
docs.text:
In the upper section of the unit editor, you can configure basic values such as walk speed, run speed, and additional settings for flying units.

Some of these values still need further investigation.

docs.title: 6. Add Audio and Effects
docs.text:
EffectSet is used for sounds and effects. There is a separate Advanced Effects Guide for the full system.

For the basic workflow, it is enough to look at audio for Attack and Spawn.

EffectSet Time also uses a normalized 0..1 range. Match the animation key and variant as well as the time when aligning a sound with a marker. 0.6 means 60% of the selected clip, not 0.6 seconds.

Use the EffectSet editor's Save to persist changes separately from the AnimationSet and locator data. Imported sound references are resource strings; the editor does not automatically package every referenced file or create a game sound bank.

For the exact fields, preview limits, sound types, and reference rules, use the Advanced Effects Guide.

docs.title: 7. Export the Unit
docs.text:
Make the root DRSModel_... collection active and choose File > Export > Battleforge Object/Unit (.drs).

  1. Choose Animated Unit for the unit metadata workflow above, or the matching Animated Object type for an animated prop. Do not export a unit as an animated object if you need its markers, unit effects, and locators.
  2. Enable Export All SKA Actions when you want the clips referenced by the saved AnimationSet written alongside the DRS. It does not mean every Blender action, and an EffectSet-only reference is not enough to select a clip.
  3. Choose Model Name Prefix explicitly. The actual default is No Prefix. Model Name Prefix, Folder Name Prefix, and Keep Existing Prefix serve different naming workflows; verify the resulting names and saved references rather than renaming output files independently.
  4. Leave [DEBUG] Export SKA Tangents enabled for Hermite tangent export unless you deliberately need a stepped/flat debugging comparison. It cannot repair missing keys or an unbaked control rig.
  5. Use the ordinary UV, normal, triangulation, mip-map, and vertex-budget checks from the object guide. Unit collision is not added by populating object collision collections; only collision-enabled animated-object types write that primitive block.

Rig export limitation: The writer exports the deform armature, not an armature whose name contains Control_Rig. It reads deform-bone location/quaternion F-curves and does not automatically bake constraints, IK, or NLA results. A successful control-rig preview is therefore not proof that the exported action contains the same motion. Prepare compatible keyed deform actions on a working copy and verify a fresh SKA import; do not destructively apply transforms or bake away the only copy of your rig.

docs.title: 8. Final Export Result
docs.text: A successful animated export produces the .drs, generated .dds maps, and the referenced .ska clips when action export is enabled. Check the message log and actual files; missing or unresolved action references must not be mistaken for a complete result.

docs.title: Animation round-trip checklist
docs.text:
• The deform armature, skin, and saved AnimationSet refer to the same model and skeleton.
  • Weights were checked across representative poses, with no more than four influences per vertex.
  • AnimationSet and EffectSet edits were saved; locator scene changes were synced.
  • Required action references resolve, and exported filenames match the chosen prefix policy.
  • Marker and sound times were interpreted as normalized fractions.
  • The exported DRS and clips were imported in a separate scene using the same Apply Transform display setting.
  • Animations were checked over their full duration, including looping and bone-attached locators, not just in a still pose.
  • Final behavior was checked in game; preview playback does not prove an external ability or sound resource is configured.

If the mesh is rotated correctly but the animation is not, inspect the deform action, rest pose, and rig/export relationships before changing GO. If a marker or locator appears in Blender but is missing from the export, check the selected model type and the relevant editor's saved metadata.
